findings.reason: The change made hook delivery pulls read the whole backlog before emitting, because a sink's Halt no longer stops paging. That is incorrect behavior in the goal-named hook page path.
The new ordered pending seek never lists a row for a reconnecting sibling binding that still has it unread. This is incorrect delivery of pending items in the goal-named ordered inbox and hook path.
A new daemon issues format-2 cursors that an old client rejects. This breaks the old-client/new-daemon compatibility that D10 names.

Model-visible AUTOMATIC_PENDING_GUIDANCE still describes pair invitations, contradicting D7. Upgrade tests and pair_accept_delivers_mixed_opening_mail_once are recorded as failing, so goal-named behavior is unverified.
The wake decision is correct under D2. The finding is an unbounded per-pass seek and a stale doc comment, which are performance hardening rather than wrong behavior.
findings.clusterOverride: The other member of seat-pending-predicate is a correctness defect in the displayed-state predicate. This one only loses the old bound on wake probes and does not change which items wake.

findings.reason: The design requires a v46-prepared, v47-retried send test. This is a missing test for the D10 stored-row migration.
The failure needs a handoff to a human-bound seat, and no real path to that was established. This is an edge-case hardening issue, not a goal-named behavior.
The prune DELETE costs time linear in thread length. This is a performance improvement and does not change correctness.

A transient capability probe failure silently downgrades the sender's chosen priority and blames the daemon version. That is a misleading result in the goal-named priority send and D10 capability-gate path.
Rust batch ordering breaks ties by SourceRank, contradicting its own doc comment and the mod's arrival-order tie-break. This is a goal-named ordering inconsistency under D11.

The mod and Rust tests pin a priority-less message, even an ACK one, as p1. D10 maps ordinary to p0 and ACK requests are p0, so this is wrong behavior against an old daemon in the goal-named ordering path.
The test-only legacy marker is a documented seam, and D6/D7 have dedicated tests. This is a coverage-hygiene improvement and does not show a missing test for goal-named behavior.
The two-pump arrival ordering exists on base. The spec only promises ordering within a batch, so this is optional hardening.
ServiceSend's receipt behavior is unchanged from base and needs a user decision. It is a documentary gap and not an incorrect behavior introduced by this change.
findings.clusterOverride: The other merge-readiness member shows concrete D7 defects (a stale guidance string and failing tests). This one is an unchanged pre-existing behavior awaiting a user decision.

findings.reason: A forward-only migration is the project norm, it exists on base, and the goal names no rollback path. This is an optional operational note.
